newsitem.title: INDIA: India says hopes Pakistan talks will improve ties.
newsitem.headline: India says hopes Pakistan talks will improve ties.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma was quoted as saying on Friday that he hoped foreign secretary-level talks with Pakistan next week would help both countries improve cool bilateral relations.

"We earnestly hope that the opportunity provided by the resumption of talks will be seized to move our bilateral relations forward," the United News of India (UNI) quoted Sharma as telling Pakistan's new high commissioner (ambassador) to India Ashraf Jehangir Qazi.
Talks between the two countries' top diplomats, stalled since January 1994, are scheduled to begin in New Delhi on March 28.
Sharma said India's approach towards the talks would be positive and constructive. "It is important at this time to look to the future and not remain mired in the past," he said.
He said cooperation between the two countries in the areas of trade, agriculture, industry, science and technology, art and culture and communications would significantly help improve relations.
Pakistan said on Friday it was willing to release all Indian fishing boats and their crew seized in its territorial waters if India reciprocated.
"We are ready to release all their boats and crew provided they also release Pakistani boats and crew," Pakistan Foreign Ministry spokesman Khalid Saleem told Reuters in Islamabad.
"We have told them this is a humanitarian issue and both countries should release all boats and crew without any pre-conditions as a humanitarian gesture," Saleem said.
Pakistani newspapers on Friday quoted the private Fisheries Cooperative Society as saying Indian coast guards had detained 34 Pakistani boats and 233 crewmen between 1993 and January 1997.
Pakistan announced last week it would free 38 Indian children held along with adult fishermen as a unilateral goodwill gesture before next week's talks.
On Thursday, India relaxed visa restrictions for Pakistani businessmen and journalists, and said Pakistani tourist groups would be allowed to visit India.
India and Pakistan both won freedom from British rule 50 years ago. The two countries have fought three wars since 1947, two of them over the disputed territory of Kashmir.
